newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says wheat area to fall, cuts soy number.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says wheat area to fall, cuts soy number.

text.p: Argentine farmers will sow an estimated 6.25 million hectares with 1997/98 wheat, down 14.9 percent from last season, the government's Agricultural Secretariat said Wednesday.

It added that it had cut its estimate for 1996/97 soybean output to 11 million tonnes from 11.48 million tonnes, but raised its 1996/97 maize production estimate to 14.7 million tonnes from 14.5 million tonnes.
The Secretariat said weather problems have delayed wheat sowing, which is only 50 percent complete so far, compared to 70 percent completion at the same stage last season.
The Secretariat added that it could alter its wheat sowing estimate either up or down depending on the weather.
Farmers should sow 258,000 hectares with brewers' barley, up 6.1 percent from 1996/97. Barley sowing is 35-percent over, compared to 47-percent completion at the same point last year.
Farmers should sow 113,000 hectares with linseed, up 20.9 percent from 1996/97. Sowing is 50 percent over, compared to only 40 percent completion at the same stage last year.
With the harvest almost completely over, total 1996/97 grain output should be a record 53 million tonnes, up 20.4 percent from last season.
Raw cotton output should be 1.0 million tonnes, the third-highest in Argentine history.
